meeting_header:
Date: 2026-05-07
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recordings: enabled
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Ava Li (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Helio Head of AI), Rohan Patel (Helio Platform), Elena Gomez (Helio Security), Jonas Meyer (Helio PM)
summary: Kickoff to scope POC for Helio Retail: align success criteria (latency p95, availability, cost target), capture workload shape (QPS, concurrency, token distribution), and define benchmark plan for hosted vs dedicated runs. Security and pilot timelines discussed; Redwood to deliver benchmark template and initial config. Customer to share anonymized traffic samples and compliance list.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, cost/1M tokens)
Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC/private
transcript: 00:00 - Samira Patel: Hi everyone thanks for hopping on, uh this is Samira from Redwood, with Diego and Ava on the call. How's everyone doing?
00:08 - Maya Chen: Hey thanks, doing well — excited to get this scoped. We want to validate Helio's chat summarization workload and a short-form product recommendation flow.
00:20 - Diego Ramos: Great, can we start with high-level goals? what are the three metrics you care about most for the POC?

00:28 - Jonas Meyer: For us it's p95 latency under 600 ms for the recommendation flow, availability 99.9% during business hours, and cost per 1M tokens below our benchmark — ballpark target $120 per 1M tokens, but that's flexible if latency improves.
00:45 - Ava Li: Helpful, thanks. Can you describe traffic shape? steady QPS or bursts, average vs peak?

00:51 - Rohan Patel: Our daytime baseline is about 35 QPS for the recommendation endpoint, with concurrency around 20. We see daily peaks up to 180 QPS for flash sales, and occasional spikes to ~300 QPS for sitewide promos, lasting around 3-8 minutes.
01:10 - Diego Ramos: So tail behavior matters — for the POC we'll include a burst profile and a steady-state profile. What about tokens per request?

01:18 - Maya Chen: Recommendation input is short — ~25-60 input tokens, output usually 60-120 tokens. The chat summarization is heavier: inputs average 450 tokens, outputs 300 tokens. There's also a retrieval step where we append ~800 tokens in the RAG context for some requests.

01:35 - Samira Patel: Good detail. For our workload sizing we'll model three profiles: low-latency short prompts, medium-size RAG requests, and long summarization. We'll need token distribution histograms — could you share anonymized samples?
01:46 - Maya Chen: Yes we'll extract histograms from logs. We prefer anonymized payloads; security will need to sign off on the transfer method.

02:00 - Elena Gomez: For security, we require SOC2 documentation, support for customer-managed KMS, and VPC peering for the dedicated/private option. SSO is Azure AD; we'll need SAML metadata. Also audit log retention 1 year.

02:18 - Samira Patel: Understood. We have SOC2 reports and support KMS/HSM integrations — we'll include those docs. VPC/private option is part of Redwood Private; for the pilot we can run hosted and a narrow dedicated test if you want to evaluate both.
02:33 - Rohan Patel: Cost question: how different is cost when you move from hosted to dedicated? We want to understand per-token delta and how to estimate our monthly run-rate.

02:42 - Diego Ramos: Typically dedicated gives better unit economics at scale and more predictable latency; we can model cost using your token mix and QPS profile. For the POC we'll run both configs and compute cost per 1M tokens including burst overhead and idle capacity assumptions.
03:00 - Jonas Meyer: What do you need from us to set up the bench?

03:04 - Ava Li: A few things: anonymized traffic samples (timestamped), desired SLA windows, which endpoints to include, and any fallbacks/mitigation logic. Also confirm whether you want model variants (e.g., smaller quantized model vs base) in the run.
03:20 - Maya Chen: We'll include two endpoints: recs (low-latency) and summarization (throughput). We'll try both a high-quality model and a quantized faster variant for the recs flow.

03:33 - Samira Patel: Great. We'll propose bench scenarios: steady-state 35 QPS for 60 minutes, burst ramp to 180 QPS for 10 minutes, sudden spike to 300 QPS for 5 minutes, and long-run summarization throughput test at 10 QPS to characterize token throughput. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
03:52 - Rohan Patel: On batching: our application uses synchronous calls and we can't afford more than 20-30 ms of queueing. How much batching is realistic?

04:00 - Diego Ramos: Continuous batching in the runtime is adaptive; for low-latency recs we'll keep batch sizes small and favor per-request latency. For throughput summarization we can increase batch sizes. We'll surface suggested batch configs for each profile.
04:14 - Maya Chen: Any specific quantization impacts on quality? We need to ensure recommendation accuracy doesn't regress more than 2-3%.
04:20 - Ava Li: We'll run a quality regression check using your eval set. Redwood Optimize can track BLEU/ROUGE or custom metrics; we'll tie quality alerts to those thresholds during the pilot.
04:33 - Elena Gomez: A quick note: we can't send raw customer PII. The anonymized histograms are fine; but if you need request traces they must be sanitized.
04:42 - Samira Patel: Absolutely — we'll accept aggregated histograms and sanitized traces only. We'll include instructions in the template.
04:50 - Jonas Meyer: Timeline: we want initial numbers within two weeks, and decision on pilot expansion within a month. Is that feasible?

04:58 - Samira Patel: Yes. We'll deliver the benchmark template by 2026-05-12 and run the initial tests between 2026-05-13 and 2026-05-26; results and cost modeling by 2026-05-28. Then we can discuss a committed Dedicated contract in June depending on outcomes.

05:12 - Diego Ramos: One challenge to call out — cold KV cache misses for RAG contexts can double latency for the first few tokens. For synthetic testing we'll include cache-warm and cold scenarios so you can see both.

05:27 - Rohan Patel: That's important. For the RAG route we do a retrieval that adds variable token counts; the worst-case is adding 1k tokens to the prompt which spikes execution time and memory pressure.
05:38 - Ava Li: We'll parameterize that in the bench: 0 tokens extra (no retrieval), 300 tokens extra (typical), and 1000 tokens extra (worst-case). We'll measure GPU memory and per-token cost.
05:50 - Maya Chen: Regarding metrics for success: beyond latency/cost, we want to measure end-to-end user perceived latency, which includes retrieval time. Can Redwood measure those traces?
05:58 - Diego Ramos: Yes, we can surface request traces and per-component timing and export traces to your telemetry (Datadog/NewRelic). We'll send example dashboards.
06:08 - Elena Gomez: Audit log question: can Redwood push full audit logs to our S3 with lifecycle rules?

06:14 - Samira Patel: Yes, log exports to S3 with encryption via your KMS and lifecycle rules are supported in Dedicated and Private; for hosted we have retention options and can stream to partner buckets under agreement.
06:26 - Jonas Meyer: Who signs the pilot SOW and what's included?

06:30 - Samira Patel: We'll send a short pilot SOW that covers benchmark runs, two model variants, security review, and one performance tuning session. It's a fixed-fee engagement to run the tests and produce the report.
06:45 - Maya Chen: Any blockers you foresee on Redwood's side?
06:48 - Diego Ramos: Only that we need the histograms and confirmation on SSO and KMS post-login details; otherwise we can run hosted tests within 24 hours of receiving configs.
07:00 - Rohan Patel: For the pilot we'll want a cron job that simulates user traffic pattern; do you provide a load harness or do we run our own?
07:07 - Ava Li: We'll provide a synthetic load harness (k6 scripts and a small runner) and a dockerized client that can replay your anonymized traces against the Redwood endpoints.
07:18 - Maya Chen: Awesome. Please include an example of the JSON payload format expected so our infra can emit the sanitized traces without extra engineering.
07:24 - Samira Patel: Will do. We'll also include notes about sequencing: warm caches first, then burst tests, then long-run steady-state.
07:33 - Jonas Meyer: Any thoughts on fallback strategies if latency spikes during promos?

07:38 - Diego Ramos: Common pattern: fallback to a smaller model, reduce max tokens, or return cached recommendations. We can also configure automatic model fallback policies with traffic shaping during overload.
07:50 - Maya Chen: That could work. We'll want to see how quality degrades when fallback happens — avoid user-facing regressions.
07:56 - Ava Li: We'll produce quality vs cost curves for the two variants so you can pick acceptable tradeoffs.
08:05 - Elena Gomez: For the private option: what's the expected on-prem resource footprint for peak 300 QPS with RAG 1k tokens?

08:14 - Diego Ramos: Rough estimate: for worst-case RAG-heavy requests you might need multiple A100-class nodes or equivalent with larger memory footprint; we'll provide a capacity planner once we have exact token distributions and model sizes. We'll include a sample capacity planning spreadsheet.
08:30 - Rohan Patel: Do you have any data retention or cache invalidation controls per customer?
08:36 - Samira Patel: Yes, cache TTLs, prefix controls, and policy-driven KV eviction are configurable. For PII-sensitive contexts we can disable KV caching for those routes.
08:47 - Jonas Meyer: Ok let's recap next steps and owners —

08:51 - Samira Patel: Recap: Samira send benchmark template & docs by 5/12; Diego deliver batching and cache recommendations 5/14; Maya provide anonymized histograms by 5/10; Elena confirm KMS/SSO and compliance list by 5/14. Weekly pilot syncs starting 5/19. Redwood will run hosted + dedicated narrow tests and present results 5/28.
09:18 - Maya Chen: Sounds good, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the template.
09:22 - Samira Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the SOW draft.
09:28 - Meeting end
